variables.policy_prompt_for_subgoal: First read the goal instruction to get the required number of placements N: if it says 'repeating this action two times' N=2, 'three times' N=3, and so on; if it mentions no repetition, N=1. The cube to use is the one whose color the goal names (ignore other cubes). Update placements_done first, then decide. An episode starts in subgoal A (pick up the cube). Rules, applied in whatever situation you are in: 1. If the goal-colored cube is shown 'is held in the gripper' at the scene of this decision step (fingers about 46% open, gripper raised), choose B: place the cube onto the target. 2. If the cube is NOT held at the scene of this decision step (fingers ~100% open) and placements_done (after this step's update) is less than N, choose A: pick up the cube, pointing at the current [y, x] of the goal-colored cube as shown in the final scene of this step (after a placement it will be sitting on or near the target; point at the cube, not the target). 3. If the cube is NOT held and placements_done (after this step's update) is equal to or greater than N, choose C: press the button to stop. 4. If the gripper closed but the cube is not reported as held (a missed grasp), treat it as not held: apply rule 2 or 3 by placements_done. If you meet a situation none of these rules cover, default to: if the cube is held choose B; otherwise if placements_done < N choose A pointing at the goal-colored cube's current position; otherwise choose C.

fields.name: placements_done
fields.description: Integer count of completed placements of the goal-colored cube onto the target. Start at 0 on the first step. At each decision step, take the value carried in; add 1 if BOTH hold: (a) at least one execution frame shown at this step has the goal-colored cube marked 'is held in the gripper', and (b) in the final scene of this step the goal-colored cube is NOT marked held, the fingers are about 100% open, and the cube lies within a few pixels of the target position. Do not require any particular finger percentage or gripper height at an intermediate frame; a release frame may show fingers only 80-90% open with the cube still marked held, and that still counts once the final scene meets (b). Do not add 1 if the cube was never marked held during this step (a missed grasp, even if the cube already rests on the target from before), or if the final scene shows the cube held. Otherwise keep the carried value unchanged. Never decrease it. e.g. 2
fields.annotation: Integer count of completed placements of the goal-colored cube onto the target so far in the episode, counting the placement shown in this step's execution steps. It is 0 at step #1 and at every step whose execution steps do not contain a release of the cube over the target. It increases by exactly one at each decision step whose execution steps show the goal-colored cube labelled 'is held in the gripper' at some frame AND whose final scene shows that cube no longer labelled held, lying within a few pixels of the target position, with the fingers ~100% open (the step whose correct subgoal follows a 'place' command). No finger percentage or gripper height is required at any intermediate frame; the 'is held' label may lag a frame behind the actual release and is ignored at intermediate frames. A step in which the gripper closed on nothing (cube never labelled held) does not count even if the cube already sits on the target from an earlier placement. A step ending with the cube held does not count. It never decreases. e.g. 2

It increases by exactly one at each decision step whose execution steps show the cube held in the gripper, then the fingers opening to ~100% while the gripper is low (height below about 0.03) at the target position, leaving the cube resting on the target (the step whose correct subgoal follows a 'place' command). It never decreases. e.g. 1

history.critique:
field placements_done, ANNOTATOR PROMPT
  Situation: the goal asked for five placements of the green cube. In one placement step the robot lowered the held cube onto the target and the frames showed the release in progress: at the lowest frame the fingers were only part-way open (around 80-90%) and the cube was still labelled 'is held', and by the frame where the fingers reached 100% the gripper had already risen above the 0.03 height. The annotated memory counted that placement (the carried-in value at the next step was one higher), but the rule as written demands one frame with fingers ~100% open AND height below 0.03, which that step never showed. This is a PREDICTABILITY fault: the rule's wording and the value written disagree at such a step. Change: the field still holds the integer count of completed placements of the goal-colored cube onto the target, never decreasing, 0 at the first step. It increases by exactly one at each decision step whose execution frames show the goal-colored cube labelled 'is held in the gripper' at some frame AND whose final scene shows that cube no longer labelled held, lying within a few pixels of the target position, with the fingers ~100% open. No condition on finger percentage or height at any intermediate frame; the intermediate 'is held' label may lag one frame behind the actual release and must be ignored. A step in which the gripper closed on nothing (fingers ~0%, cube never labelled held) does not count even though the cube already sits on the target from an earlier placement. A step that ends with the cube held (a pick-up) does not count. e.g. 2

field placements_done, POLICY PROMPT
  Situation: same as above; the policy, following the instruction literally, found no frame with both fingers ~100% open and height below 0.03 (the low frame had fingers ~87% open and the cube still marked held; the fully-open frame was already raised) and so kept the count at 1 where the annotation had 2. PREDICTABILITY fault. Change: integer count of completed placements, start at 0 on the first step, never decrease. At each decision step take the value carried in and add 1 if BOTH hold: (a) at least one execution frame shown at this step has the goal-colored cube labelled 'is held in the gripper', and (b) in the final scene of this step the goal-colored cube is NOT labelled held, the fingers are about 100% open, and the cube lies within a few pixels of the target position. Do not require any particular finger percentage or height at an intermediate frame; a release frame may show fingers only 80-90% open with the cube still labelled held, and that still counts once the final scene meets (b). Do not add 1 if the cube was never labelled held during this step (a missed grasp, fingers closed to ~0%, with the cube already resting on the target from before). Do not add 1 if the final scene shows the cube held. e.g. 2
